etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English medicacioun, from Middle French médication and its etymon Latin medicātiō, from medicārī (“to heal, cure”), from medicus (“a physician, surgeon”), from medērī (“to heal”).

definitions.definition: A medicine, or all the medicines regularly taken by a patient.

quote.citation: 2019 March 19, The Great Stand Up to Cancer Bake Off, season 2, episode 3, Michael Pennington (actor), via Channel 4:
quote.text: Are you going to be be like this all day? It’s like I’ve not took[sic – meaning taken] my medication.
